instruction: For each date in the calendar spreadsheet whose day is a multiple of 5, set the cell's background color to orange and leave all other dates as they are.

metadata.explanation: Task requires highlighting all dates where day % 5 == 0 in orange. Verified with Python: 30 cells identified (5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th, 30th of each month). Custom getter extracts background colors from these cells, custom metric compares against expected orange color with tolerance.

llm_judge_reasons: POSITIVE: Complete coverage - getter extracts background colors from ALL date cells, categorizing them into div5_cells (dates divisible by 5) and non_div5_cells (other dates). This enables full verification of both requirements.
POSITIVE: Negative validation implemented - metric checks that non_div5_cells do NOT have orange background (lines 69-84), fulfilling the 'other cells remain unmodified' requirement.
POSITIVE: Positive validation implemented - metric verifies all expected div5 cells ARE highlighted with orange (lines 58-66).
POSITIVE: Completeness check - metric verifies that all expected cells were found by the getter (lines 86-97), penalizing if cells are missing.
POSITIVE: Color matching semantically correct - uses fuzzy matching with tolerance (default 20) to handle slight color variations, which is appropriate for real-world verification.
POSITIVE: Final score uses min(positive_score, negative_score) - ensures BOTH conditions must pass for high score.
POSITIVE: Postconfig properly saves file with Ctrl+S to ensure state is persisted.
MINOR: Getter dynamically discovers cells, so if spreadsheet layout differs from expected, completeness check will catch discrepancies.
